_README: Bio clause templates. THIS IS THE FALLBACK PATH, NOT THE PRIMARY ONE.
The primary engine for bio text is a language model conditioned on the personality the
deterministic layer produces. This pool exists so the tool keeps working when no model
is reachable, and so load-test populations at scale do not need one.
IT IS DELIBERATELY SMALL AND DELIBERATELY PLAIN, and that is the whole design.
A read of two hundred generated profiles found ten defect classes, every one of them a
property of this file rather than of the composition code: calqued German idiom
('arbeite an Kochen'), compounds no German speaker forms ('Buchbinden-Verteidiger'),
ASCII stand-ins for umlauts, lower-cased German nouns, conversational replies used as
self-descriptions ('Zurzeit keine Fragen'), meaningless fragments ('orbit', 'null',
'echo'), and register whiplash inside one language. Making a template set produce good
varied prose in two languages is the part that failed, and it is not attempted again.
RULES FOR ANYONE EDITING THIS FILE:
1. Every clause is a SELF-DESCRIPTION. Not a greeting, not a reply, not a mood.
'Not currently accepting questions' is a chat message; nobody's profile says it.
2. Each language is AUTHORED IN THAT LANGUAGE, never translated from the English set.
If a form does not exist naturally in the target language, it does not go in.
3. Plain over clever. No idiom, no register experiments, no jokes that date.
4. NO EM-DASH, EN-DASH OR HORIZONTAL BAR, and no separator a phone keyboard cannot
produce. This was already the standing rule (CCB-S3-021) when an em-dash was
authored into the separator pool anyway. A generated bio is member-facing output,
so the rule always covered it; what did not cover it was verify:no-dashes, which
scanned the bot's own copy and not this tree. It does now.
The reason is not typographic taste: a member cannot type an em-dash on a phone,
so a profile containing one advertises that the text was machine written, which is
exactly what this generator exists to avoid. The middle dot went the same way for
the same reason rather than by the same rule. The test is what a member can type,
not which characters a list happens to name.
5. A WRONG BIO IS WORSE THAN NO BIO. Two thirds of real profiles have none, so
silence is always available and always realistic. When in doubt, leave it out:
the template path runs at a raised empty rate for exactly this reason.
`allowLowercase` is per language because the lower-case habit is an English habit.
German capitalises nouns, so lower-casing a German bio is not a style but a spelling
error, and the mechanism was applied to German unchanged.
